Produced by Bulova under their budget-friendly Caravelle brand during the late 1960s to early 1970s, this timepiece features an early electronic/transistorized movement. This technology bridged the gap between traditional mechanical wind-up watches and the modern quartz movements that followed. • Dial & Face: Soft champagne sunburst dial featuring gold-tone baton indices, a central crosshair design, and a stylized "infinity" Caravelle logo. It is cleanly marked "TRANSISTORISED" above the 6 o'clock position. • Case & Crystal: Classic round gold-tone mid-century case with a distinct manual winding and time-setting crown at the 4 o'clock position. • Band: Fitted with a period-accurate, flexible metal expansion "stretch" band in a matching gold-and-silver tone. • Movement: Powered by an early electronic balance-wheel mechanism that utilizes a battery rather than a mainspring to keep time, offering a continuous sweeping second hand. rows.t: TOULOUSE LAUTREC RARE 1954 LITHO PRINT FRENCH EXHBT POSTER AT MOULIN ROUGE 1892

det.desc: DESCRIPTION: 1954 TOULOUSE-LAUTREC “OEUVRE GRAPHIQUE” — GALERIE DES PONCHETTES, NICE — MOURLOT LITHOGRAPHIC EXHIBITION POSTER An especially interesting piece from this collection: the 1954 lithographic exhibition poster for Oeuvre graphique de Toulouse-Lautrec at the Galerie des Ponchettes in Nice, France. The exhibition was held from January 30 through March 15, 1954 at Galerie des Ponchettes, 77 Quai des États-Unis, Nice, and was devoted to Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec’s graphic work. The official City of Nice heritage record identifies the exhibition poster as a 1954 production by Mourlot in Paris. This particular example was purchased at the exhibition itself in 1954 and has remained with the same six-piece group of Toulouse-Lautrec lithographs acquired there. THE IMAGE The poster incorporates Toulouse-Lautrec’s imagery from Au Moulin Rouge, featuring La Goulue and her sister, together with the exhibition typography and information for the Galerie des Ponchettes. Rather than simply reproducing one of Lautrec’s commercial posters, this sheet was specifically created to announce the 1954 Nice retrospective, making it an artifact of the exhibition itself. det.desc: The product is a framed and signed print of the painting "State Of Mind" by artist Demarcus McGaughey. Demarcus McGaughey (b.1975) a Texas native and New York-based mixed media artist, passionately captures the beauty, strength, and vibrancy of people of color. McGaughey also pays homage to cultural influences with elements of pop art, mass media, comic books, and advertising in his pieces. Inspired by Barkley Hendricks, who famously painted Black people in all their coolness, McGaughey portrays his people in a larger-than-life display. Drawing inspiration from Andy Warhol’s acclaimed artistry in pop art and advertising along with Kehinde Wiley’s massive masterpieces, McGaughey’s work exudes an undeniable flow. The print, measuring 14 inches in height and 11 inches in width, features urban art, contemporary art, pop art, and graffiti art themes. The artwork incorporates neo-expressionist text elements reminiscent of Jean-Michel Basquiat's signature style, including phrases like "Black Lives Matter," "Gifted," and "Power." This limited edition print is numbered 3 out of 11 and is on paper material. The framing and signature add value to this unique artwork from the United States.
